checks: At full dimension m, Borell's s=1/m endpoint is a constant positive density on convex support. Finite mass and an interior ball force bounded support, since an escaping sequence would create disjoint interior midpoint balls.

Positive neighborhoods give support Minkowski inclusion. At interior inputs, their small-ball combination remains inside the target support. Comparing ball volumes gives a linear radius inequality, and sending all but one source radius factor to zero gives c_j≥c_{z_i} separately for each positive incidence.

Conversely the supported portions E_i∩Q_{z_i} have positive Lebesgue mass and their Minkowski combination lies in Q_j and in the original test sum. Ordinary Brunn–Minkowski with the constant-density inequalities proves the full compact-test claim.

The same-support example with constants 1,2,1 verifies that equality of densities does not follow. Prism heights satisfy the anchored Minkowski inclusions and their projected ordinary volume is the prescribed constant-density law.

If the original total ordinary volume tends to zero and an original fiber has a positive common-normalized weak limit, any bounded Hausdorff subsequential fiber limit contains that weak support. Full support dimension m would force a positive limiting volume by continuity, a contradiction. These are the endpoint and vanishing-mass clauses of b9e8ea5c75ef1e0e §6.

overlap.comparison: The accepted graph result treats q<N; its positive hidden block and density-root argument do not give the q=m density-max criterion or prism.

Its bounded actual thin sequence already gives the q<m exclusion after Hausdorff convergence. The new endpoint result additionally treats arbitrary full-dimensional compatible measure incidences, and its exclusion requires only a subsequence chosen from bounded fibers.

readability: The prism preserves the given density with ordinary volume in dimension m+1. The dimension restriction in the vanishing-mass case refers to the original continuous coordinate space.
